title: Excel final exam question set

questions.prompt: Which practice makes a workbook easier to maintain?
options: Use clear sheet names, structured headers and a source/calculation/output separation.
Merge all cells across every data row.
Keep formulas and source values mixed without labels.
Delete raw source records after each refresh.
questions.answer_key: Use clear sheet names, structured headers and a source/calculation/output separation.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: When a formula is copied down and a rate cell must stay fixed, which reference style is appropriate?
options: A purely relative reference such as F1.
An absolute reference such as $F$1.
A reference to the entire workbook without a cell address.
A text label instead of a reference.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What should you do when a formula returns an unexpected result?
options: Wrap every formula in IFERROR and ignore it.
Check ranges, input types, precedents and intermediate values, then compare with an expected result.
Change the output number manually.
Assume the source data is always correct.
questions.answer_key: Check ranges, input types, precedents and intermediate values, then compare with an expected result.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: How should a threshold rule be tested?
options: Only at a typical mid-range value.
Below, exactly at and above the threshold.
Only after hiding the formula.
Only on a chart.
questions.answer_key: Below, exactly at and above the threshold.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: Why preserve a raw copy before cleaning customer data?
options: To compare before/after values and recover the original values if needed.
Because raw values must never be validated.
To make duplicate removal random.
To replace identifiers with row numbers.
questions.answer_key: To compare before/after values and recover the original values if needed.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What helps avoid locale ambiguity when importing dates?
options: Trust any text that looks like a date.
Set/verify the date locale and inspect a known sample after import.
Convert every date to a two-digit year.
Store all dates as arbitrary display strings.
questions.answer_key: Set/verify the date locale and inspect a known sample after import.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What is a key lookup reliability check?
options: Confirm matching data types, unique keys when expected, and not-found behavior.
Sort the return array randomly.
Assume identifiers with leading zeros are numeric.
Use approximate matching without checking its rules.
questions.answer_key: Confirm matching data types, unique keys when expected, and not-found behavior.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What can cause a dynamic-array formula to return a spill error?
options: Occupied cells block part of the intended output range.
The workbook has more than one sheet.
The formula is in the formula bar.
The cells have headers.
questions.answer_key: Occupied cells block part of the intended output range.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: Which source-table pattern is most robust?
options: One header row, consistent columns and data types, no spacer rows inside the table.
Multiple title rows embedded between records.
Merged column headers and subtotals mixed into the raw rows.
Inconsistent names for the same field.
questions.answer_key: One header row, consistent columns and data types, no spacer rows inside the table.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What makes a chart usable for a reader?
options: A descriptive title, clear units/time period, readable labels and a suitable chart type.
Only decorative colors.
No title or labels.
Three-dimensional effects regardless of data.
questions.answer_key: A descriptive title, clear units/time period, readable labels and a suitable chart type.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What should be checked after refresh?
options: Filters, aggregation logic, source range and totals against source records.
Whether the chart colors changed.
Only whether the PivotTable still exists.
Whether the raw data can be removed.
questions.answer_key: Filters, aggregation logic, source range and totals against source records.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What is the safe sequence when consolidating monthly tables?
options: Confirm schemas/types, append compatible rows, refresh and reconcile row counts/totals.
Append all files without inspecting columns.
Rename dates as text and ignore failures.
Overwrite the raw file with the transformed output.
questions.answer_key: Confirm schemas/types, append compatible rows, refresh and reconcile row counts/totals.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What must be validated before relying on a measure over related tables?
options: Relationship keys/cardinality and measure results against a control total.
Whether table names are visually short.
Whether the source has cell borders.
Whether all tables have the same number of rows.
questions.answer_key: Relationship keys/cardinality and measure results against a control total.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What belongs in a trustworthy financial model?
options: Explicit assumptions, units/periods, independently checked calculations, sensitivity cases and limitations.
Hidden assumptions and overwritten outputs.
A single forecast without alternative scenarios.
Manual values pasted over formulas.
questions.answer_key: Explicit assumptions, units/periods, independently checked calculations, sensitivity cases and limitations.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What is the right role of Excel Accessibility Checker?
options: Use it plus manual review of reading order, labels, contrast and keyboard access.
Treat a clean checker result as a guarantee of full accessibility.
Remove all table headers.
Use color alone to show pass/fail.
questions.answer_key: Use it plus manual review of reading order, labels, contrast and keyboard access.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What does worksheet protection not replace?
options: Access controls and secure handling of sensitive data.
Preventing accidental edits to locked cells.
Clear documentation.
Validation checks.
questions.answer_key: Access controls and secure handling of sensitive data.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What should you check before choosing an automation tool?
options: Target environment, file/tenant policies, required API support and execution permissions.
Assume VBA and Office Scripts run identically everywhere.
Enable unknown macros automatically.
Skip testing to prevent differences.
questions.answer_key: Target environment, file/tenant policies, required API support and execution permissions.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.

questions.prompt: What should a spreadsheet change process retain?
options: Ownership, version history, input validation, tests, approval and retirement/archival notes.
Only the last saved value and no history.
Private credentials embedded in cells.
Formulas replaced by manual totals.
questions.answer_key: Ownership, version history, input validation, tests, approval and retirement/archival notes.
questions.explanation: The correct choice is the one that makes assumptions explicit, preserves data integrity, checks expected results and respects Excel/version/security constraints.
